tests.name: Numerical Reasoning Test 6
tests.subtitle: AssessmentDay source test
tests.description: A 30-question numerical reasoning practice test using product sales, equity funds, maintenance costs, furniture sales, graduate salaries and retail competitor data.
tests.instructions:
This numerical reasoning test comprises 30 questions, and you will have 30 minutes in which to correctly answer as many as you can. Calculators are permitted for this test, and it is recommended you have some rough paper to work on.

You will have to work quickly and accurately to perform well in this test. If you don't know the answer to a question, leave it and come back to it if you have time. Each question will have five possible answers, one of which is correct. You may click Back and Next during the test to review or skip questions.

You can submit your test at any time. If the time limit is up before you click submit the test will automatically be submitted with the answers you have selected. It is recommended to keep working until the time limit is up.

Try to find a time and place where you will not be interrupted during the test. The test will begin on the next page.

questions.prompt: Which of the products shown had the lowest value of sales per non-European store and which had the highest value of sales per European store?
questions.explanation: Non-European sales per store are DE45 $2,500, PU20 $2,222.22, AE25 $2,166.67, PU10 $4,800 and FD24 $1,285.71, so FD24 is lowest. European sales per store are DE45 €807.69, PU20 €1,578.95, AE25 €2,227.27, PU10 €2,077.78 and FD24 €1,130.77, so AE25 is highest.

questions.prompt: What is the discrepancy (in $) between the AE25 price per product unit in non-European stores compared to European stores. Use an exchange rate of €0.80 to the $.
questions.explanation: The European AE25 price is €200 ÷ €0.80 per $ = $250. The discrepancy from the non-European $130 price is $250 − $130 = $120.

questions.prompt: This month’s combined target for non-European and European sales of AE25 is €40,000. Using an exchange rate of €0.75 to the $, what is the difference between the sales values shown and this target?
questions.explanation: Convert non-European AE25 sales: $13,000 × €0.75/$ = €9,750. Combined sales are €9,750 + €24,500 = €34,250, so the target shortfall is €40,000 − €34,250 = €5,750.

questions.prompt: Combining European and non-European sales, which products generated the highest number of product units sold? Use the non-promotional sales prices shown.
questions.explanation: Using sales ÷ regular unit price, combined units are DE45 = 35,000/175 + 21,000/150 = 340; PU20 = 287.5; AE25 = 222.5; PU10 = 330; FD24 ≈ 213.33. DE45 is highest.

questions.prompt: Given that a customer uses the promotional offers shown, put the 5 products sold in non-European stores into order of increasing promotional price per unit (starting with the cheapest).
On the previous day, the value of the shares held in the Emerging Markets Fund was 0.5% lower than the values given here. What was the previous day’s value of shares in the Emerging Markets Fund?
questions.explanation: Current shares value is 50% of £38.9m = £19.45m. The previous day was 0.5% lower: £19.45m × 0.995 = £19.35275m, or £19.35m.

questions.prompt: Which out of the Emerging Markets, UK and Far Eastern funds hold the lowest value of Cash and the lowest value of Bonds?
questions.explanation: Cash values are Emerging Markets £3.89m, UK £5.56m and Far Eastern £7.86m, so Emerging Markets is lowest. Bond values are Emerging Markets £11.67m, UK £11.12m and Far Eastern £3.406m, so Far Eastern is lowest.

questions.prompt: Which equity fund has the highest average value per individual investor?
questions.explanation: Average values per investor are UK £55.6m/3,450 ≈ £16,116; US £24.3m/1,460 ≈ £16,644; European ≈ £15,812; Far Eastern ≈ £16,635; Emerging Markets ≈ £14,624. The US Fund is highest.

questions.prompt: Which of the components of the UK and US equity funds have the highest and the lowest value?
options: lowest is US Fund (Bonds); highest is UK Fund (Derivatives)
lowest is US Fund (Shares); highest is UK Fund (Shares)
lowest is UK Fund (Bonds); highest is US Fund (Shares)
lowest is US Fund (Bonds); highest is UK Fund (Shares)
lowest is US Fund (Derivatives); highest is UK Fund (Shares)
questions.explanation: UK component values are Cash £5.56m, Bonds £11.12m, Derivatives £16.68m and Shares £22.24m. US values are Cash £4.86m, Bonds £3.645m, Derivatives £2.43m and Shares £13.365m. Lowest is US Derivatives and highest is UK Shares.

questions.prompt: Which equity fund holding(s) hold less than double the number of Shares compared to Bonds?
questions.explanation: Compare percentage holdings because each comparison is within one fund. UK Shares 40% equal twice Bonds 20% (not less); US Shares 55% exceed twice Bonds 15%; Emerging Markets Shares 50% are less than twice Bonds 30% (=60%).

questions.prompt: Averaged across the Manufacturing Plants, put the average values for each of the maintenance costs in decreasing size order, starting with the highest.
options: Servicing, Administration, Misc., Rent, Insurance, Utilities
Servicing, Administration, Rent, Misc., Utilities, Insurance
Servicing, Administration, Rent, Misc., Insurance, Utilities
Servicing, Administration, Misc., Rent, Utilities, Insurance
questions.explanation: Column averages are Servicing £1,000, Administration £589, Misc. £450, Rent £295, Insurance £192.20 and Utilities £185.80. That gives the order in option A.

questions.prompt: For which manufacturing plant(s) are the Administration: Rent costs in the ratio 12:5?
questions.explanation: Bordeaux has 600:250 = 12:5, and Glasgow has 720:300 = 12:5. No other plant has this ratio.

questions.prompt: For the Glasgow manufacturing plant, which maintenance cost(s) represent approximately 7% of the total costs?
questions.explanation: Glasgow's total is 195 + 875 + 300 + 189 + 720 + 425 = £2,704. Insurance is 195 ÷ 2,704 × 100 = 7.21%, and Utilities is 189 ÷ 2,704 × 100 = 6.99%. Both are approximately 7%, so the answer is Insurance and Utilities.

questions.prompt: What is the average annual cost for servicing each of the 5 manufacturing plants (assume 4 weeks in a month)?
questions.explanation: Average weekly servicing is (1,050+1,100+950+1,025+875)/5 = £1,000. At 4 weeks × 12 months = 48 weeks, annual average cost is £1,000×48 = £48,000.

questions.prompt: Which two manufacturing plants have the same total maintenance costs per week?
questions.explanation: Weekly totals are Midlands £2,816, Bordeaux £2,790, Berlin £2,451, Amsterdam £2,799 and Glasgow £2,704. No two are equal.

questions.prompt: Which garden furniture manufacturer has 22.5% of the UK market in terms of 2010 annual sales?
questions.explanation: Total sales are £1.2m+£3.3m+£2.4m+£2.7m+£2.4m = £12m. Manufacturer D has £2.7m/£12m = 22.5%.

questions.prompt: Manufacturers B and D each aim to increase their annual sales from 2010 to 2011 by a quarter. Manufacturers A, C and E each aim to grow their annual sales by a fifth. Assuming all companies meet these targets, what will be 2011’s total furniture manufacturer sales (to the nearest £million)?
Which region showed the second largest absolute difference in Company C sales between 2009 and 2010?
questions.explanation: Absolute changes are Northern £34,000, Central £73,700, Southern £44,300, Eastern £47,600 and Western £23,000. Eastern is second largest.

questions.prompt: What is the percentage increase in Company C’s total sales for 2010 compared its 2009 total sales?
If Company C’s sales in 2009 were in the ratio of 8:7 for online: offline sales, what were the offline sales (to the nearest £1,000)?

Assume that the percentage change trends between the Current Year and Next Year continue at the same rate for a subsequent year. What’s the subsequent year’s average entry level graduate salary (to the nearest £500)?
questions.explanation: The chart gives one average salary for each sector but does not give the number of graduates in each sector. Without those sector weights, the overall average graduate salary cannot be calculated or projected; averaging the five sector averages would incorrectly assume equal graduate counts.

questions.prompt: In Year 3 a company paid the average entry graduate starting salaries when recruiting 15 graduates for a consultancy role and 6 graduates for a research role. What was the average salary per recruited graduate?
Which sector has seen the smallest percentage increase in graduate entry level salary between Year 2 and the Current Year?
questions.explanation: Percentage increases are Engineering 0.8/23.7=3.38%, Research 0.7/23.5=2.98%, Consulting 0.7/27.6=2.54%, Legal 3.4/29.8=11.41%, and Accounting 0.7/26.6=2.63%. Consulting is smallest.

questions.prompt: The current year’s entry level graduate salaries for working in logistics and retail are £25,000 and £24,000 respectively. If these sectors experience the same percentage change as the legal sector over the same period, what’s next year’s predicted entry level graduate salary in the logistics and retail sectors (to the nearest £100)?
questions.explanation: Legal rises from £33.2k to £34.3k, a factor of 34.3/33.2 = 1.03313. Logistics: £25,000×1.03313 ≈ £25,800; retail: £24,000×1.03313 ≈ £24,800, both to the nearest £100.

questions.prompt: Which of the 5 sectors had the lowest difference in entry level graduate salary between Year 3 and the Current Year?
questions.explanation: Differences are Engineering £0.4k, Research £0.7k, Consulting £1.3k, Legal £2.3k and Accounting £0.3k. Accounting is lowest.

questions.prompt: Which competitor(s) has less than 100,000 customers per day (assume 30 days per month)?
questions.explanation: Daily customers are A 4.2m/30=140,000; B ≈73,333; C=150,000; D≈103,333; E≈73,333. Only B and E are below 100,000.

questions.prompt: Which Competitor has the lowest average number of staff per country of operation?
questions.explanation: Staff (thousands) per country are A 325/38=8.55, B 180/30=6, C 295/22=13.41, D 204/28=7.29 and E 154/32=4.81. Competitor E is lowest.

questions.prompt: If Competitors B to E make up 85% of the business sector in which they operate (based upon operating profits), approximately what are the total operating profits of the other companies in the same business sector?
questions.explanation: B–E operating profits total £45.4m+£56.5m+£42.9m+£42.7m = £187.5m, representing 85%. Sector total = £187.5m/0.85 = £220.59m; the other 15% is £33.09m, approximately £33m.

questions.prompt: Competitor B has an additional business that generates an additional 8% to the Retail Sales shown. Competitors A and C have additional businesses that generate 7% and 4% additional revenue respectively. What’s the total of these additional sales streams for Competitors A, B and C combined (to the nearest £million)?
questions.explanation: Additional sales are A £57.4m×7%=£4.018m, B £52.5m×8%=£4.2m and C £68.2m×4%=£2.728m. Total £10.946m rounds to £11m.

questions.prompt: Which two Competitors average the same approximate number of customers per country of operation?
questions.explanation: Monthly customers per country (millions) are A 4.2/38=0.1105 and D 3.1/28=0.1107, approximately equal. The other values are B 0.0733, C 0.2045 and E 0.0688.

questions.prompt: Which country has the largest number of males in employment?
questions.explanation: Male employment counts (millions) are Belgium 10.4×35.6%=3.7024, Denmark 5.4×58.2%=3.1428, Ireland 4.1×38.8%=1.5908, Hungary 10.1×38.4%=3.8784 and Greece 10.8×34.4%=3.7152. Hungary is largest.

questions.prompt: What percentage do the five countries shown represent of the total EU population?
questions.explanation: The five populations sum to 10.4+5.4+4.1+10.1+10.8 = 40.8 million. As a percentage of 480 million: 40.8/480×100 = 8.5%.

questions.prompt: Assuming that there are no other population factors than those shown in the table, what will be the annual population change of the five countries combined?
questions.explanation: Net rates per 1,000 are Belgium 11.1−9.8+3.4=4.7, Denmark 2.6, Ireland 20.1, Hungary 4.5 and Greece 3.2. Changes are 48,880 + 14,040 + 82,410 + 45,450 + 34,560 = 225,340.

questions.prompt: If the population of Belgium increases at the same %age rate as shown for 2012, in what year will the population reach 10.6 million?
questions.explanation: Belgium's net annual rate is (11.1−9.8+3.4)/1,000 = 0.47%. Starting at 10.4 million on 1 Jan 2012, four years of growth gives 10.4×1.0047^4 ≈ 10.597 million, which is 10.6 million to the table's one-decimal precision in 2016.

questions.prompt: Which country has the largest absolute difference in the number of people dying compared to the number of people being born?
questions.explanation: Absolute birth/death count differences are Belgium 1.3×10.4m/1,000=13,520; Denmark 9,180; Ireland 8.3×4.1m/1,000=34,030; Hungary 27,270; Greece 1,080. Ireland is largest.

questions.prompt: In which month were PT Drinks sales one-third that of total sales?
questions.explanation: In May, total sales are 114+120+108 = $342,000, and PT Drinks has $114,000. Since 114/342 = 1/3, May is correct.

questions.prompt: If Kurnels continued to increase its sales at the same percentage rate as between April and May, what would Kurnels’ sales be in August (to the nearest $1,000)?
questions.explanation: The April-to-May factor is 108/68 ≈ 1.5882. Applying it for June, July and August gives $108,000×(108/68)^3 ≈ $432,681 (about $433,000 mathematically). The source's intended and closest listed choice is $432,000.

questions.prompt: What was the difference between the total sales of Kurnels and those of Diapon between February-May?
questions.explanation: Kurnels February–May total is 56+86+68+108 = $318,000. Diapon's is 76+60+108+120 = $364,000. Kurnels is smaller by $46,000.

questions.prompt: Between which months did Kurnels show the greatest change in its proportion of total sales?
questions.explanation: Kurnels' monthly proportions are 53/161=32.92%, 56/206=27.18%, 86/226=38.05%, 68/274=24.82% and 108/342=31.58%. The largest adjacent change is 38.05% to 24.82%, between March and April.

questions.prompt: If the three soft drinks manufacturers experience the same proportional increases in sales between May-June as between April-May, what will be the combined sales for the three soft drinks manufacturers in June (to the nearest $1,000)?
questions.explanation: June projections are PT 114×114/98=132.61, Diapon 120×120/108=133.33 and Kurnels 108×108/68=171.53 (all $000s). Total = $437.47k, which rounds to $437,000.

questions.prompt: A trader bought 150,000 shares in Hydro Tools at this month’s low and 250,000 shares in Gel Products at this month’s high. What is the trader’s profit or loss if he sells all the shares at today’s prices? (Assume that there are no dealing charges).
Yesterday, which share was the furthest from its yearly low in absolute terms?
questions.explanation: Yesterday minus yearly low is LPC £0.30, Hydro £0.25, Gyromanic £0.59, Flyer £0.22 and Gel £0.45. Gyromanic is furthest.

questions.prompt: How many shares of LPC Ltd and Flyer Travel Ltd can a trader buy today who spends £2.1 million and splits the value of the shares in the ratio of 2:5 respectively (ignoring any other taxes or charges incurred)?
questions.explanation: Allocate £2.1m in a 2:5 ratio: LPC gets £600,000 and Flyer gets £1.5m. Shares bought are £600,000/£2.40 = 250,000 LPC and £1.5m/£2.50 = 600,000 Flyer.

questions.prompt: How much would the loss be from buying 125,000 Gyromanic shares at this month’s high, then selling all the shares at this month’s low?

Yesterday, Trader A spent £650,000 purchasing LPC Ltd shares and Trader B spent the same amount on Flyer Travel shares. If Trader A and Trader B each sold their entire shareholding today, how much more profit would Trader B make than Trader A?
questions.explanation: Trader A bought 650,000/2.60=250,000 shares and loses £0.20 each, a £50,000 loss. Trader B bought 650,000/2.27≈286,343.61 shares and gains £0.23 each, £65,859.03 profit. B's profit exceeds A's by £115,859.

questions.prompt: Which competitor, or competitors, are predicted in the Next Quarter to achieve sales of less than its average over Quarters 1-4?
questions.explanation: Q1–Q4 averages are A $10m, B $10.25m, C $13.25m, D $11m and E $10m. Next-quarter values below those averages are B at $10m and C at $13m.

questions.prompt: Assuming that the Next Quarter’s projection is accurate, but that in all subsequent Quarters sales drop by 5% each quarter, by how much will Competitor D’s sales in Year 2 exceed those of Year 1 (to the nearest $10,000)?
questions.explanation: Competitor D's Year 1 total is 11+15+8+10 = $44m. Year 2 is 12 + 12×0.95 + 12×0.95² + 12×0.95³ = $44.5185m. Excess = $0.5185m, which rounds to $520,000.

questions.prompt: Competitor C operates 18 stores compared to Competitor E’s 15 stores. How much more sales revenue would Competitor E have needed to make to match Competitor C’s average sales per store in Quarter 1?
questions.explanation: Competitor C averages $12m/18 = $0.6667m per store. Across 15 stores, E would need $10m; E made $9m, so it needed $1m more.

questions.prompt: In the Next Quarter Competitors A and B merge their sales operations, and in response Competitors C and D decide to operate together. Competitors A and B exceed their projected quarterly sales by 2/9ths. Next Quarter’s sales for Competitors C and D are in line with their averages over the previous 4 quarters. What is the value of the combined sales of Competitors A-E for the Next Quarter, to the nearest $million ? (Assume that Competitor E’s projected sales for the next quarter are correct).
questions.explanation: A+B projected sales are $21m; exceeding by 2/9 gives $21m×11/9=$25.667m. C and D use averages of $13.25m and $11m; E is projected at $11m. Total = $60.917m, rounding to $61m.

questions.prompt: Which competitor has a ratio of 4:5 Quarter 4 : Quarter 3 sales?
questions.explanation: Competitor C has Quarter 4:Quarter 3 sales of 12:15, which simplifies to 4:5.

questions.prompt: What was the difference in the value of FLAC product sales compared to BEC product sales?
Which product code has the highest profit margin? (Assume Profit margin = Sales price – Production costs).
questions.explanation: Per-unit total costs are £3.26, £3.38, £3.28, £3.59 and £3.63 respectively. Margins are £0.99, £0.77, £1.52, £1.06 and £1.32. FLAC 3X is highest.

questions.prompt: What would have been the additional sales revenue on BEC 5C units if all those that had been produced in January were sold?
questions.explanation: Unsold BEC 5C units are 6,500−4,800 = 1,700. Additional revenue at £4.15 each is 1,700×£4.15 = £7,055.

questions.prompt: If the labour, design and Misc costs for producing the FLAC 9Y decrease by 5%, 7.5% and 12.5% respectively, what will be the profit when selling 25,000 FLAC 9Y units?
questions.explanation: Adjusted costs per 100 are £150×0.95=£142.50, £101×0.925=£93.425 and £108×0.875=£94.50, totaling £330.425, or £3.30425 per unit. Profit on 25,000 at £4.65 is (£4.65−£3.30425)×25,000 = £33,643.75. The source's intended and closest listed choice is £33,642.50.

questions.prompt: An order valued at £14,350 is placed for FLAC 4T units at a sales price that is £0.85 below the norm. What is the profit on this order?
questions.explanation: Discounted price is £4.95−£0.85 = £4.10, so the order contains £14,350/£4.10 = 3,500 units. FLAC 4T costs (164+105+94)/100 = £3.63 per unit. Profit = (£4.10−£3.63)×3,500 = £1,645.

questions.prompt: For the company which achieved the highest sales per number of their stores in France, what was their sales value across the five countries combined?
questions.explanation: France sales per store are Wellings €20m/3=€6.67m, Seacombe €25m/6=€4.17m, Tillings €15m/3=€5m, Kingleys €25m/5=€5m and Astors €5m/11≈€0.45m. Wellings is highest; its five-country sales total 35+25+20+15+15 = €110m.

questions.prompt: The economic recession is predicted to decrease the total retail sales in Germany, Ireland and Italy by 7.2%, 9% and 4.6% respectively. What total sales value is predicted in Germany, Ireland and Italy combined?
questions.explanation: Country totals are Germany €100m, Ireland €105m and Italy €125m. After decreases: 100×0.928 + 105×0.91 + 125×0.954 = 92.8+95.55+119.25 = €307.6m.

questions.prompt: Which two countries have the same average sales across the five retail companies?
questions.explanation: Country totals are UK €90m, Ireland €105m, France €90m, Germany €100m and Italy €125m. Dividing each by five preserves equality, so France and the UK have the same average (€18m).

questions.prompt: What would be the value of the UK and the French sales in £ (assume an exchange rate of €1.25 to the £)?
questions.explanation: UK and France each total €90m, so combined sales are €180m. At €1.25 per £, value in pounds is €180m/1.25 = £144m.

questions.prompt: Wellings Ltd sells off its Italian stores and then takes over Seacombe’s stores except those in Ireland. The merged Wellings Seacombe Ltd sets a target to increase total sales across the European stores by 20% a year for the next three years. What will the total sales be in three years’ time (to the nearest million)?
questions.explanation: Wellings total is €110m; removing Italy's €15m leaves €95m. Acquired Seacombe sales excluding Ireland are €10m+€25m+€30m+€30m = €95m. Starting total €190m grows to €190m×1.2³ = €328.32m, or €328m.
